evidence.section: 2.1. LPBF process and post heat treatment
evidence.quote: The parameters for the LPBF process are as follows: a layer thickness of 0.03 mm, laser power set to 250 W, scanning speed of 1000 mm/s, and a scanning spacing of 0.14 mm. An intra-layer path planning strategy utilizing strips with a width of 5 mm was employed, with an inter-layer rotation angle of 67 ◦ and a preheating temperature of 100 ◦ C.
Metallographic analysis reveals that the as-deposited samples have a regularly arranged structure of equiaxed β phases, with an average grain size of approximately 100 μ m.
the top surface is composed of a series of regularly arranged equiaxed grains, while the side surface consists of columnar grains whose growth direction is parallel to the build direction.

evidence.quote: alongside the precipitate free zone (PFZ) of similar width observed on either side of the continuous α grain boundary.

The specimens exhibited an increasing trend in hardness with the progression of heat treatment processes, including annealing, solution treatment, and aging. However, with prolonged aging time, the hardness of the specimens decreased.

the as-deposited LPBF TC17 samples exhibit low strength and high ductility, which can be attributed to the rapid solidification process and the dispersion strengthening effect of the ultra-fine αs during the LPBF process.

The increase in the average β grain size from 100 μ m to 126 μ m indicates that during the annealing process, some smaller β phases gradually dissolved while other β grains experienced growth, resembling the Ostwald ripening process [18].
